about.lead: Kashi Tamil Sangamam celebrates the civilisational bond between Tamil Nadu and Kashi. It was conceived as an expression of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat: two of India's oldest centres of learning, Kashi on the Ganga and the Tamil country on the Vaigai and the Kaveri, meeting to rediscover shared traditions of language, scholarship, faith, craft and cuisine.
about.p1: KTS 5.0 takes the Thirukkural, the 1,330 couplets of Thiruvalluvar, as its unifying theme. The couplets speak of virtue, wealth and love in a language that every Indian tradition recognises as its own, which is why the Central Institute of Classical Tamil has translated the text into all twenty-two languages of the Eighth Schedule.
about.p2: Under this theme, 1,000 Participating Institutions across India, selected by the Nodal Institutions of the States/UTs, each assess their interested students on the Thirukkural and nominate one on merit; the selected students take part in a two-lecture academic orientation in their own language and a one-month research and academic engagement, write an article or research note of at least 4 and not more than 10 pages under a Faculty Supervisor/Guide, and carry the text back to their campuses through a one-hour presentation of their own.
about.who1: The Ministry of Education is the nodal ministry for the Sangamam.
about.who2: The Central Institute of Classical Tamil, Chennai, implements KTS 5.0: this portal, on which institutions register and the Participating Institutions nominate their students, the multilingual orientation, the digital repository, apps, films, publications and outreach to schools.
about.who3: IIT Madras and Banaras Hindu University are the nodal and coordinating institutes on the Tamil Nadu side and the Kashi side.
about.who4: Indian Railways, the Airports Authority of India, the National Highways Authority of India, the Ministry of Culture, UGC, AICTE, CBSE, KVS and the Governments of Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh are partners for displays, outreach, travel and venues.
about.caption: Thiruvalluvar, author of the Thirukkural
about.j1: More than 2,500 people from Tamil Nadu, from twelve walks of life, visited Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya on eight-day tours. Organised by the Ministry of Education with the Government of Uttar Pradesh at Banaras Hindu University.
about.j2: Held at Namo Ghat, Varanasi, with interactive academic sessions between professionals from Tamil Nadu and Kashi, and real-time Tamil translation of the inaugural address through an app.
about.j3: Bridging Indian knowledge and tradition with contemporary discourse, and highlighting the legacy of Sage Agasthyar; 1,200 participants, including 200 students of Tamil origin from central universities.
about.j4: “Let us learn Tamil”: fifty Tamil teachers taught in the schools of Varanasi, 300 students from Varanasi studied Tamil in colleges in Tamil Nadu, and the Agasthya Expedition travelled from Tenkasi to Kashi. The valedictory function was held at Rameswaram.
about.j5: “Thirukkural Payilvom”: the Thirukkural for every campus in India, in every Indian language.

prog.i1.d: This website: a single place for programme administration, the registration of institutions, the nomination of students, content delivery and coordination among the participating agencies. It carries the registration of institutions, the nomination of students by the Participating Institutions, the candidate portal, the digital repository and the coordination hub of the partners.
prog.i2.d: A fully accessible repository of learning materials and research assets: the Thirukkural in the Indian languages and in foreign languages, research publications, the Thirukkural Multilingual App, the Thirukkural Ground-Truth Corpus of palm-leaf manuscripts, and related websites.
prog.i3.d: A campaign across India, through the Nodal Institutions of the States/UTs, academic institutions, digital media and partner universities, invites institutions to the programme. The institutions register on this portal; the Nodal Institution of each State/UT selects the number of Participating Institutions prescribed for it, 1,000 in all, and each of them registers the student it has nominated.
prog.i3.l2: Eligibility: students of the selected Participating Institutions
prog.i3.l3: One student nominated on merit by each Participating Institution
prog.i4.d: Each selected Participating Institution assesses its interested students on their interest in and understanding of the Thirukkural, by a short written test (the portal offers an online test, in the language each student chooses), an oral interaction, a presentation, an essay, a quiz or a combination of these, and nominates one student on merit. The Nodal Institutions and CICT then verify the nominations.
prog.i5.d: A two-part series of academic video lectures on the Thirukkural, offered in the 22 scheduled languages, Tamil among them, and in English (23 languages in all): translated, dubbed or subtitled, delivered language by language, with a 20-minute live question-and-answer segment in each session.
prog.i6.d: The selected students undertake a one-month research and academic engagement: structured study with CICT's multilingual study material, educational videos and academic orientation. Each eligible selected student is entitled to a stipend of ₹10,000, subject to the programme guidelines and completion of the prescribed requirements.
prog.i7.t: Student presentation and dissemination of knowledge
prog.i7.d: Each selected student prepares an original article or research note of at least 4 and not more than 10 pages under the guidance of a Faculty Supervisor/Guide, and presents the research at the institution during the engagement period in a one-hour presentation or lecture on the Thirukkural, with a PowerPoint (PPT) or another suitable presentation, so that each of the 1,000 campuses hears the couplets from one of its own students; the institution submits its video recording to CICT. The student and the institution post the news of KTS 5.0 on the student's social media and arrange for it to appear on the college's website and social media and in the local news media.
prog.a1.d: All 1,330 couplets with the translations of CICT into the 22 scheduled languages, two Tamil commentaries, English prose, word-level grammar, metrical analysis and references to palm-leaf manuscripts. It works offline, carries no advertisements, and is released under the CC BY 4.0 licence.
prog.a2.d: Twenty-minute lectures on selected couplets in Indian languages, explaining their meaning, values and relevance, published on the YouTube channels of CICT and on this portal.
prog.a3.d: Recitations of the couplets with meanings, explanations and translations in several languages, designed for visually impaired students, for those who learn by listening, and for audiences who do not know Tamil.
prog.a4.d: Recitation of the entire text, couplet by couplet, with the Tamil commentary of Dr Mu. Varadarajan, for correct pronunciation and for the study of the three sections.
prog.a5.d: Fifteen-minute films that dramatise selected couplets on ethical leadership, social harmony, truthfulness, gratitude and civic duty, screened at KTS venues, on campuses and by broadcasters.
prog.a6.d: Animated videos of sixty to ninety seconds on individual couplets, made with the help of artificial intelligence, with subtitles in many languages, published every day on the social media channels of CICT.
prog.a7.t: Annual National Conference on the Thirukkural
prog.a7.d: Held in major cities with the Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti and Banaras Hindu University, bringing together scholars and translators from every language region.
prog.a8.d: Couplets with translations on passenger information systems and signboards at railway stations, airports and highway toll plazas, in coordination with Indian Railways, the Airports Authority of India and the National Highways Authority of India.
prog.a9.d: Illustrated stories for children inspired by the Thirukkural, first in English and Hindi, distributed through school boards and available for download from this portal.
prog.a10.d: Print-ready posters in many languages for schools, colleges and libraries, distributed to CBSE, KVS, JNV and state school networks, and available for download.
prog.b1.d: A calendar of couplets for 200 school days, one for each morning assembly, with the translation and meaning in the language of the school, distributed as printed flip-charts and as digital packages.
prog.b2.d: Collections of scripts, guides to narration and ideas for the stage, so that students present the values of the Thirukkural through stories, speeches, skits, plays and dance-dramas.
prog.b3.d: Crosswords, puzzles, complete-the-line games, memory pairs, word-guessing and typing challenges, with interfaces in many languages and levels from beginner to scholar.

nodal.how_title: How the programme reaches the institutions
nodal.p1: In view of its standing and coordinating capacity, one higher educational institution in each State or Union Territory is designated as the Nodal Higher Educational Institution. All interested higher educational institutions register on this portal; the Nodal Institution scrutinises them and selects the number of Participating Institutions prescribed for its State or Union Territory, in accordance with the Standard Operating Procedure, with due regard to institutional readiness, outreach capacity, geographical spread and representation, and keeps a reserve list. It nominates a senior officer as the State/UT Nodal Officer, coordinates the nomination and registration of the students, facilitates the assessments and the orientation, and monitors the timely completion of the activities.
nodal.p2: Each selected Participating Institution assesses its interested students on the Thirukkural, nominates one student on merit with one Faculty Supervisor/Guide, with the endorsement of the Head of the Institution, and submits the nomination on this portal.
nodal.p3: The Nodal Institutions and CICT verify the nominations. The selected students, one from each Participating Institution, join the Inaugural and Valedictory Functions online and take part in the academic orientation and the one-month research and academic engagement.
nodal.p4: Participating institutions may also organise academic and cultural activities based on the Thirukkural, such as essay writing, quizzes, debates, elocution, recitation, storytelling, poster-making and presentations, for wider student engagement. A brief report on the activities undertaken is submitted to CICT and the Ministry in the prescribed format (Annexure-IV of the D.O. letter of 31 October 2026).

guide.title: How to take part
guide.intro: Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 – Thirukkural Payilvom reaches students through their institutions: each selected Participating Institution assesses its interested students and nominates one on merit. Here is what each one does, step by step.

guide.s1_t: Check that your institution takes part
guide.s1: Only a selected Participating Institution can nominate a student. Look for yours in the list of Participating Institutions. If your institution is not registered, ask its Head to register it by {hei_end}; the Nodal Institution of your State/UT then selects the Participating Institutions from those registered, and registration does not by itself confer selection.
guide.s2: By {camp_to}, your institution assesses its interested students. If it uses the portal's online test, your Institutional Coordinator gives you its link and access code: {questions} questions in {minutes} minutes, in the language you choose.
guide.s3: Your institution selects one student on merit and informs the selected student by e-mail.
guide.s4: Your Institutional Coordinator submits your nomination on the portal. Give the coordinator a photograph, an ID proof and your details; the nomination form is signed and sealed by the Head of your institution, with the details of your Faculty Supervisor/Guide. You receive your application number by e-mail.
guide.s5: The Nodal Institution of your State/UT and CICT verify your nomination, and CICT informs you by e-mail and on this portal. Follow your application on the Application status page.
guide.s6: You join the Inaugural and Valedictory Functions of KTS 5.0 online, take part in the academic orientation and the one-month research and academic engagement, write an article/research note of at least 4 and not more than 10 pages with your Faculty Supervisor/Guide, deliver a one-hour presentation at your institution, and are entitled to a stipend of ₹10,000, subject to the programme guidelines and the completion of the prescribed requirements. The dates are on the Schedule.
guide.i1: Register your institution with the details of the Head of the Institution, the Institutional Coordinator and the Faculty Supervisor/Guide. If your Nodal Institution has invited your institution, complete the registration from the invitation e-mail. The Nodal Institution of your State/UT selects the Participating Institutions by the Standard Operating Procedure; registration does not by itself confer selection.
guide.i2_t: Sign in to the institution's page
guide.i2: Sign in with the e-mail address of the Institutional Coordinator or of the Head of the Institution. A six-digit code is mailed to you; there is no password.
guide.i3: Switch on the portal's online test, choose its days, and give your students its link and access code; you see every student's score, ranked. You may also assess them in any other suitable mode. The process is to be fair, documented and approved by the Head of the Institution or an authorised committee.
guide.i4: Select the student on the institution's page, from the ranked list or by entering a student assessed in another way. The portal informs the student by e-mail.
guide.i5: On the institution's page, fill in and submit the nomination form of the student: a photograph, an ID proof, the nomination form signed and sealed by the Head of the Institution, and the details of the Faculty Supervisor/Guide. The page then shows the application number.
guide.i6: Organise Thirukkural activities for all your students, such as essay writing, quizzes, recitation, storytelling and poster-making, and send a brief report to CICT in the prescribed format (Annexure-IV).
guide.n1: CICT creates the console account of the Nodal Officer of each State/UT from the details furnished by the Nodal Institution. You sign in to the console with your e-mail address.
guide.n2: Under Institutions in the console, scrutinise the institutions registered for your State/UT, record the marks of the evaluation committee under the Standard Operating Procedure (Annexure-V), and select the number that Annexure-I prescribes, with a reserve list, by {hei_select_end}. The list of the selected institutions downloads in the format of Annexure-II, to be furnished as the final list. Each institution is informed by e-mail.
guide.n3: The Progress page of the console shows which institutions of your State/UT have assessed their students, selected one and registered them, with their coordinators. The portal reminds those that are behind, and you can remind them too.
guide.n4: In the verification queue of the console, check each student's photograph, ID proof and nomination form, and verify the application or reject it with a remark.
guide.n5: See that the Participating Institutions of your State/UT and their students join the Inaugural and Valedictory Functions online; monitor the articles/research notes, the one-hour presentations and the records, and submit the consolidated report of your State/UT as prescribed.

disp.intro: Open one of these links on a screen at an airport, a railway station, a metro station or train, a bus stand or bus, or a campus. The banner keeps itself up to date: the time of India from the portal's clock, a Thirukkural couplet that changes on a schedule and is the same on every screen at the same moment, and the countdown to Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0. disp.k.countdown.d: Days, hours, minutes and seconds to Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0, and then the day of the programme.

nl.b4: By {papers_due} the article or research note, the activity report and the recording are submitted to CICT as prescribed; the portal will carry the manner of submission.
nl.b5: The Nodal Institution, the Participating Institutions and the nominated students join the Inaugural Function on {kts_start} and the Valedictory Function on {kts_end} virtually; the joining link will be communicated separately.
nl.p5: Each eligible selected student is entitled to a stipend of ₹10,000, subject to the programme guidelines and completion of the prescribed requirements. It is disbursed directly to the student through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) after CICT verifies the outputs, subject to validation of the student's bank account details by the Participating Institution through the CICT portal. Please keep the selected student's bank details ready for that validation when the portal asks for it; the stipend page of the portal ({portal}/stipend) explains the steps.
nl.p6_t: Resources on the portal, free and in 23 languages.
nl.p6: The study book of 108 couplets with their meanings ({portal}/syllabus); all 1,330 couplets of the Thirukkural in 22 languages ({portal}/thirukkural); the study companion ({portal}/companion); a practice test and a classroom quiz for the campus ({portal}/practice, {portal}/quiz); the orientation lectures ({portal}/orientation); posters for the notice board ({portal}/posters); the Schedule and the Ministry's letter ({portal}/schedule, {portal}/notices); and a video guide for Participating Institutions ({guide}).
nl.p7: Besides the nomination, Participating Institutions are encouraged to hold Thirukkural-based activities on the campus during the Sangamam: essay writing, quiz, debate, elocution, recitation of the couplets in Tamil and in the students' own languages, storytelling, posters, a Thirukkural wall or a reading hour. The classroom quiz of the portal puts the questions on the screen and takes the answers on the students' phones. Photographs and a short note on these activities may be sent to this office for the consolidated report of the State/UT, and posted on the institution's social media with the hashtags #KashiTamilSangamam #KTS5 #ThirukkuralPayilvom.
nl.p8: For the portal: {contact_email}, {contact_phone} ({portal}/contact). For the programme: the Registrar, CICT, Chennai, registrar@cict.in. For {state}: {name}, Nodal Officer, {email}, {phone}.

ng.committee_src: Standard Operating Procedure, Annexure-V of the letter
ng.g1: The Head of each Nodal Institution shall constitute an Evaluation Committee.
ng.g2: The Committee shall consist of at least three members, including the State/UT Nodal Officer.
ng.g3: The Committee shall evaluate all eligible applications and award marks according to the criteria and scoring parameters in Paragraph 3 of the Standard Operating Procedure.

hs.title: Submitting the selected student on the portal
hs.lead: How the Institutional Coordinator of each Participating Institution nominates its student on the portal by {date}, and how the Nodal Officer of the State/UT selects the institutions and verifies the nominations. The screens named below are in English.
hs.coord: For the Institutional Coordinator of a Participating Institution
hs.c1: Open {inst_login} and enter the e-mail address of the Institutional Coordinator or of the Head of the Institution given at registration. Type the six-digit code that the portal mails to you; it is valid for 15 minutes. There is no password.
hs.c2: The institution's page shows the status of your institution. The assessment and the nomination open once the Nodal Institution has selected it as a Participating Institution.
hs.c3: Assess the interested students by {date}. To use the portal's online test, go to {online_test}, choose the days and the syllabus, press {switch_on} and give your students the link and the access code; their scores appear on the page, ranked, and {excel} downloads them. You may also assess them in any other suitable mode. The process is to be fair, documented and approved by the Head of the Institution or an authorised committee.
hs.c4: In {students_list}, press {select} beside the student chosen on merit. For a student assessed in another way, fill in the student's name (in English letters), e-mail, mobile number, roll number, course and language under {selected} and press {send_link}.
hs.c5: The portal informs the student by e-mail. Press {open_reg} and fill in the student's nomination form by {date}: a photograph, an ID proof, the nomination form signed and sealed by the Head of the Institution, and the details of the Faculty Supervisor/Guide; then submit it.
hs.c6: Once the nomination is submitted, the page shows the application number and its status, and you and the student receive an e-mail. The Nodal Officer of your State/UT then verifies the application.
hs.c7: Until the nomination is submitted, {withdraw} cancels the selection so that you can select another student. After that, write to CICT.
hs.nodal: For the Nodal Officer of the State/UT
hs.n1: Open {nodal_login} and sign in with the e-mail address and password of the Nodal Officer account that CICT created for you; change the password at the first sign-in.
hs.n2: Under {institutions}, scrutinise the institutions registered for your State/UT, record the marks of the Evaluation Committee with {marks}, and select the number prescribed in Annexure-I with {select_inst}, with a reserve list ({reserve}), by {date}. {annex2} downloads the list of the selected institutions in the format of Annexure-II.
hs.n3: {progress} shows, for each Participating Institution of your State/UT, whether it has assessed its students, selected one and submitted the nomination, with its coordinator; you can remind those that are behind. {progress_excel} downloads the whole list.
hs.n4: In {queue}, open each application, check the photograph, the ID proof and the nomination form, and press {verify}, or {reject} with a remark, by {date}.
hs.n5: Under {applications}, the {excel} and {csv} buttons download the list of the students of your State/UT, with the filters you have chosen.
ng.screen: Only the applications found eligible after scrutiny (identity, location, recognition/affiliation, AISHE/Institution Code where applicable, official contact details and the approval of the competent institutional authority) are placed before the Evaluation Committee; curable deficiencies may be corrected within the notified scrutiny period.
ng.replace: If a selected institution declines, remains non-responsive or fails to nominate a student by the notified deadline, the next eligible institution from the approved reserve list may be included. Every replacement is recorded with reasons and approved by the State/UT Nodal Officer or the competent authority before it is communicated to CICT.
ng.own_method: A Nodal Institution may adopt its own transparent and objective methodology for the selection, keeping in view the objectives and broad principles of the Standard Operating Procedure; the methodology adopted is documented and communicated to CICT.
